LESSON: GUIDED READING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Reading 2.3 Reading Aloud (2 lessons) • Vocabulary Expansion • Fluency (speed an
Topic 2.5: Guided Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What clues can help you comprehend a text?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. recite key words, expressions and phrasesin simple texts
2. show awareness of the importance of correct articulation when reading texts

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED READING
Subject: MANDARIN · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided Reading helps you succeed in MANDARIN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GUIDED READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Recite key words, expressions and phrasesin simple texts

What this means
In this part you learn to recite key words, expressions and phrasesin simple texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recite key words, expressions and phrasesin simple texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recite key words, expressions and phrasesin simple texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Show awareness of the importance of correct articulation when reading texts

What this means
In this part you learn to show awareness of the importance of correct articulation when reading texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: show awareness of the importance of correct articulation when reading texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Reading to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can show awareness of the importance of correct articulation when reading texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided Reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: recite key words, expressions and phrasesin simple texts)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Reading to a partner. (skill: show awareness of the importance of correct articulation when reading texts)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided Reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: recite key words, expressions and phrasesin simple texts.
3. Practise this skill: show awareness of the importance of correct articulation when reading texts.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Guided Reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided Reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Guided Reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What clues can help you comprehend a text?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided Reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: recite key words, expressions and phrasesin simple texts.
5. Be able to: show awareness of the importance of correct articulation when reading texts.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
